key_insight: A synthetic, periodic large-scale structure introduced in the outer region of a turbulent boundary layer can drive phase-locked large-scale motions near the wall and modulate turbulence intensity through top-down interactions.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a controllable way to probe and potentially manipulate boundary-layer turbulence by targeting outer-layer structures that influence near-wall dynamics.
method: Active plasma actuator placed in the outer layer to generate a spanwise-uniform synthetic large-scale structure
Planar particle image velocimetry and spanwise-offset hot-wires used over a long downstream region
Phase-locked analysis applied to isolate large-scale motion development and turbulence-amplitude modulation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong correlation between near-wall large-scale motions and periodic turbulence-amplitude modulation, with phase-dependent changes in production and transport observed in the measurements.
watch_item: The near-wall cycle effects were transient and spanwise coherence changes were intermittent, so the actuator-induced control may be limited in durability and robustness.
paper_title: Response of a Turbulent Boundary Layer to a Synthetic Periodic Large-Scale Structure
